C08-M01-L03-F1.title: The alert lifecycle: from detection to feedback
C08-M01-L03-F1.caption: An alert moves through generation, queueing, triage and investigation to a disposition; each disposition leads to its own action, every path ends in a closure record, and feedback returns to detection.
C08-M01-L03-F1.alt: Graph diagram. Generated leads to Queued and prioritised, then Triage, then Investigate, then a decision Disposition?. Triage can also lead straight to the decision. The decision branches to True positive, which leads to Escalate to incident response; Benign true positive, which leads to Close with documented reason; False positive, which leads to Close and tune the rule; and Undetermined, which leads to Monitor and record the gap. All four actions lead to Closure record. A dashed Feedback arrow runs from Closure record back to Generated.
C08-M01-L03-F1.note: Every path ends in a closure record, and every closure can send feedback to the detection layer.
